usageNotes: Use this to modify an existing SDN fabric's protocol settings, IP prefix ranges, or routing parameters. The fabric must already exist; use the POST endpoint to create one. Changes take effect after running the SDN apply operation — the PUT itself returns null synchronously, not a task UPID. Requires SDN.Allocate on /sdn/fabrics/{id}; supply the current config digest to prevent race conditions when multiple operators may be editing simultaneously.

examples.summary: Update a WireGuard fabric to enable persistent keepalive for NAT traversal

tips: The 'delete' and 'redistribute' params are marked required in the spec even when empty — always pass them as empty arrays if not removing/adding entries.
After updating a fabric, call POST /cluster/sdn (apply) to push the config to all nodes; without apply the change is staged but not active.
Pass 'digest' (retrieved from GET /cluster/sdn/fabrics/fabric/{id}) to guard against concurrent modifications in multi-admin environments.
Protocol-specific params only apply to their respective protocol: 'area' and 'redistribute' for OSPF/Openfabric, 'csnp_interval'/'hello_interval' for Openfabric, 'persistent_keepalive' for WireGuard.
The 'lock-token' param is only needed when the global SDN config is locked by another operation — typically not required for normal updates.
